question: Should OpenClaw carry this private, harness-neutral standalone CLI and portable-schema package in the core monorepo during incubation, or should the work remain in the RFC/separate-package path until its public ownership is chosen?
rationale: The branch adds a 36-file experimental package and command surface whose stated future npm identity and host scope are intentionally undecided; that placement decision cannot be resolved mechanically from the patch.

options.title: Sponsor core incubation
options.body: Keep the private packages in this monorepo, after fixing the parser compatibility regression and defining the review boundary for future adapters.

options.title: Keep it RFC-owned for now
options.body: Move the incubation work out of the core tree until maintainers select a durable package, repository, and ownership model.

options.title: Narrow to schema extraction
options.body: Land only a clearly shared portable-schema seam if maintainers need it now, and defer the standalone CLI until its product boundary is approved.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core incubation
recommendation.body: Keep the private packages in this monorepo, after fixing the parser compatibility regression and defining the review boundary for future adapters.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the evidenced contributor for the proposed Claws package split, although a current-main area owner should confirm the final direction.
